feedback.problem: Find all values of $c$ that satisfy the mean value theorem for integrals for  $f(x)=3{x}^{2}$ on the interval $[-2,2].$
feedback.worked_solution:
Applying the mean value theorem for integrals, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(c)(b-a) & ={\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\ f(c) & =\frac{1}{b-a}{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2-(-2)}{\int }_{-2}^{2}3{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{1}{4}\cdot ({x}^{3})|}_{-2}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[{2}^{3}-(-2)^{3}] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot 16 \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the expression for $f(x)$ to solve for the value of $c:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(c) & =4 \\ 3{c}^{2} & =4 \\ {c}^{2} & =\frac{4}{3} \\ c & =\pm \frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}.\end{aligned}
$$
